Forty channels. Two cycles. Two hundred thousand cells.
Before analysing a single one, one click asks Plexora AI to check the whole slide.
Plexora measures every channel itself: focus, alignment between cycles, and segmentation. The AI is shown only what code can't settle.
First, it audits all forty channels at a glance. Nineteen are clean.
For each check, it looks at real places across the score, and decides whether the cut-off sits in the right place.
Here, a bright blob on the tissue edge, in cycle one only. Debris. It is traced, and its cells are excluded.
Down here, the edge is red, with no green: tissue lost before the second cycle. Excluded too.
These CTLA4 fibres are just as bright in the nuclear stain. That's autofluorescence, not staining.
The deposits beside them, it can't be sure about. So it leaves them for you.
Segmentation errors are flagged too, each with a reason you can read.
Before it closes, it checks its own work, and takes a second look at three regions.
About nine minutes, start to finish. Every call is an annotation you can edit. Nothing is deleted.
